youtube.title: Your Cat Likely Can't Taste Sweet or Sugar: 1 Broken Gene 🐱 (Things Living In Your House #64)
youtube.description:
Can cats taste sweet things or sugar? In cats, one gene of the sweet taste receptor (Tas1r2) is broken, so cats most likely can't taste sugar; the one tiger and one cheetah the researchers tested had the same broken gene. In a small 2020 study, cats were more likely to approach an unfamiliar person who slow blinked at them.

#cats #catfacts #meatballmyths #shorts

Sources: Li et al. 2005, PLoS Genetics; Humphrey et al. 2020, Scientific Reports.

youtube.title: Moose Injure More People Than Bears in Alaska 🫎 (Would Meatball Survive? #2)
youtube.description:
What should you do if a moose charges? Alaska's Department of Fish and Game says more people in Alaska are injured by moose than by bears each year. A charging moose often kicks forward with its front hooves. Unlike with bears, running is usually a good idea because a moose won't chase you very far, and if one knocks you down, curl up, protect your head and hold still until it moves away.

#moose #alaska #meatballmyths #shorts

Sources: Alaska Department of Fish and Game (Aggressive Moose); U.S. National Park Service (Moose Safety). General information, not safety training.

youtube.title: 14 Dogs Tested: Your Dog's Guilty Look May Not Be a Confession 🐶 (Things Living In Your House #65)
youtube.description:
Why do dogs look guilty? In a 2009 test of 14 dogs, owners told the dog not to eat a treat and left the room. The "guilty look" was no different whether or not the dog had eaten it. It showed up more when owners scolded, and the effect of scolding was stronger in dogs that had obeyed. In a 2015 study of 96 dogs, owners did no better than chance at telling from the greeting whether their dog had eaten the food. These studies test the look, not what dogs feel.

#dogs #guiltydog #meatballmyths #shorts

Sources: Horowitz 2009, Behavioural Processes; Ostojic, Tkalcic & Clayton 2015, Behavioural Processes.

youtube.title: You Can't Outrun a Grizzly Bear: It Can Run as Fast as a Racehorse 🐻 (Would Meatball Survive? #3)
youtube.description:
Can you outrun a grizzly bear? The U.S. National Park Service says bears can run as fast as a racehorse, uphill and down, and that they will chase fleeing animals like dogs do, so do not run. If a grizzly attacks, the Park Service says to play dead: flat on your stomach, hands clasped behind your neck, pack on. Alaska's bear-safety guide narrows that to a defensive bear that has knocked you down, and calls it rarely necessary. If the attack keeps going, or the bear stalked you then attacked or attacked in your tent, fight back. Per the Park Service, a black bear attack is different: do not play dead. The Park Service also says no single strategy works in every situation.

#grizzlybear #bears #meatballmyths #shorts

Sources: U.S. National Park Service (Staying Safe Around Bears); Glacier National Park (Bear Safety); Alaska Department of Fish and Game (Framework for Bear Safety Messages). General information, not safety training.

youtube.title: Your Cat Can Likely Tell Its Name: Under 1 in 10 Even Meowed 🐱 (Things Living In Your House #66)
youtube.description:
Do cats know their names? In a 2019 study, a hidden speaker played four ordinary words and then the cat's own name. Cats that had settled down during the other words reacted more to their own name. More than half answered by moving their ears and heads; fewer than 10% meowed, moved their tail or took more than a step. Cats living in a cat cafe could not tell their own name from the names of the other cats there. The study did not test whether cats come when called.

#cats #catfacts #meatballmyths #shorts

Source: Saito, Shinozuka, Ito & Hasegawa 2019, Scientific Reports.

youtube.title: Shark Attacks 2025: 65 Confirmed Unprovoked Bites Worldwide 🦈 (Would Meatball Survive? #4)
youtube.description:
How many shark attacks were there in 2025? The International Shark Attack File confirmed 65 unprovoked shark bites on people worldwide in 2025, nine of them fatal, counted 29 provoked bites separately, and says the chances of being bitten remain extremely low. Its tips: swim with a buddy and not at dawn or dusk. If a shark comes close, keep eye contact, move away slowly and leave the water if you can. If it bites, hit the eyes and gills, and do not act passively.

#sharks #sharkattack #meatballmyths #shorts

Source: International Shark Attack File, Florida Museum of Natural History (2025 yearly summary; Quick Tips; Advice to Swimmers). General information, not safety training.

youtube.title: Your Dog's Tail Wag May Lean to Its Right When It Sees You 🐕 (Things Living In Your House #67)
youtube.description:
Dog tail wag meaning: what does it mean when a dog wags its tail more to the left or the right? A 2024 review in Biology Letters says wagging is lopsided: dogs lean the wag to their own right for things they like, such as their owner, and to their own left for things that make them pull back, such as an unfamiliar, dominant dog. In a 2013 study, dogs watching videos of a left-leaning wag had higher heart activity and acted more anxious than with a right-leaning wag. It is a lean, not a rule: wagging goes with good and bad excitement, and a robot-dog study did not fit the simple story. A wagging tail does not always mean a dog is friendly.

#dogs #dogbodylanguage #meatballmyths #shorts

Sources: Leonetti et al. 2024, Biology Letters; Siniscalchi et al. 2013, Current Biology; Artelle et al. 2011, Laterality.
